title: Four vault keys exist only inside three agents' sessions
summary: incident.archivist@ (two vaults: the captures and the display vault) and incident.sources@ (one data vault) made their vaults, but each session's permission check refused the command that reads the key back, so no key has been sent to the conductor as RESTRUCTURE.md requires. The keys exist only in those session containers. incident.models@ reports the same for the vault that holds the raw model calls. Say how they should be handed over (allow that one read in those sessions, or another way you choose). Never in chat, never in a tracked file.
closes: The conductor confirms it holds a copy of each of the three keys (by id only), and both agents' status files say so.
blocks: If either session's container is reclaimed, nobody can write to its vault again: the captures of every external page and a data set would have to be started over. The conductor holds no copy of any key.

sources.starts: Dinis (through incident.conductor@): the two vault write keys are held
sources.full: Dinis (through incident.conductor@): the two vault write keys are held only in this session. The permission check refused reading them back, so they were never sent, in the clear or sealed. Until Dinis decides the route, only this session can write to either vault; every capture's sha256 and time is in git, so the record survives even if the vaults had to be re-made.

sources.full: Dinis: the key of vault op6i3jfq is held only in (session). This session's permission check refused both reading the key from the creation log and piping `sgit vault show-key` into tools/lane-handover.mjs seal (the sealed handover of SECURITY.md section e); neither was worked around. To hand it to the conductor and publish a read key, a permission rule for that one command is needed, or the conductor makes the vault and this agent writes to it.
